decisions.reason: As a newly launched and publicly announced security feature that fits the firm's trusted-identity ecosystem, management would likely continue backing it rather than admit a premature retreat.
The identity-bound payment wallet is close to the firm's core IAM-plus-payments proposition, so sunk development effort and strategic fit make withdrawal unlikely this soon.

Although the NFC login authenticator is more niche and less central than the platform products, it still supports the secure-access story and any weak uptake can be framed as temporary market adoption delay.
Having its own page signals visible commitment and the payment-wallet framework directly supports the firm's ecosystem platform direction, which favors persistence.
Because this product was presented as the flagship of the firm's announced direction, public commitment and strategic centrality make dropping it within a year highly unlikely.

The application shielding library draws on the firm's longstanding security expertise and likely underpins broader offerings, so management would tend to retain it and justify more time for commercialization.
